Established marathon preparation must retain substantial support under this supplied 75 km baseline; this is not a universal minimum.
Each recovered established-marathon taper week retains a smaller current-fitness work dose, bounded below the specific-block dose.
Background main-lift volume and deadlift effort reduce near the marathon.
Eight-week marathon from an 18 km baseline must not become approved just to satisfy the date.
Bench-only default support lifts receive maintenance/technique rather than a separate progressive peak, unless explicitly overridden.
Fixing support lifts must retain demanding bench competition practice.
Day-after-half lower lifting is absent or deliberately reduced, rather than unchanged maintenance.
An unrelated strength deload must not cause a lower-lifting rebound in the running race week.
A dated future handover is planned subject to actual recovery review, not presented as proof of recovery.
Changing observed recovery from 24 to 96 hours must affect dose or an explicit review warning.
Changing observed long-run duration must affect dose or an explicit review warning.
Repeating the same known marathon date in another supported field must not change the prescription.
Eligible repeated same-lift evidence influences calibration/review of a newly requested proposal; approved records remain separate.
